Subject: Re: Production errors: EU payment flows failing / 502/503/504 spikes

Eva — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We see the same signature in our observability (EU LB pool). I've opened a PagerDuty incident (PD-4567) and we've stood up a triage bridge. Short answers: this appears to be an ingress load-balancer amplification causing 502/503s and secondary 429s from our downstream routing.

Immediate next steps (we're executing now):
- Triage bridge active (link in follow-up)
- Temporarily route Clearline traffic to our EU-2 standby pool to reduce LB pressure
- Throttle noisy prefixes for a short window and enable stricter concurrency limits for this tenant
- Collect KV/edge logs and capture backend traces for 30m window

I'll keep you updated every 15 minutes. If you have a preference for traffic diversion (region fallback vs. queued retry), say so now; otherwise we'll start EU-2 diversion and reduce client-visible retries.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12 08:40:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Clearline EU spike — actions & asks (PD-4567)

Team — summary from triage: starting ~07:30 UTC we have a large bump in short-lived connections to the EU edge LB for Clearline's tenant. Symptoms: increased 502/503/504 from proxy layer, followed by 429s as backends enforce rate limits. Hypothesis: a combination of a client burst plus a mis-optimized LB ring causing slow accept/health-check oscillation (amplifies retries).

Ask list (owner in parens):
- Triage logs & kv cache dump for 07:20-08:20 UTC and upload to shared drive (Tessa)
- Temporarily flip routing for tenant clearline-bank to EU-2 standby pool (Tessa)
- Add temporary per-tenant concurrency cap to limit cascading retries (Jonas)
- Prepare communication blurb for Clearline explaining fallback and expected ETA (Marissa)
- Evaluate whether a kernel-level accept backlog misconfiguration contributed (Grace)

Mitigation notes: diversion to EU-2 should reduce proxy 502s quickly; we should avoid a full rollback of recent LB optimization changes unless we see persistent repeat after diversion. We'll maintain a 1.5 hour watch and then propose a postmortem.

Attaching: PD incident id, snapshot and traffic dump (see attached).

— Marissa

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12 09:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Internal: Clearline EU spike — actions & asks (PD-4567)

On the bridge we completed the EU-2 diversion at 08:55 UTC. Initial telemetry post-diversion:
- Proxy 502/503 rate for Clearline dropped from ~17.8% -> 3.4% in the first 6 minutes
- 429s observed dropped by ~60% once concurrency cap enforced
- Overall latency p50 improved ~220ms for affected routes

What we changed:
1) Updated per-tenant routing rule to route clearline-bank to eu-2-standby pool
2) Applied a temporary concurrency cap = 10 (was unlimited for this tenant) at edge LB for 30 minutes
3) Tuned proxy accept backlog on eu-frontline nodes (increase from 128 -> 512) while we validate kernel-level behavior

We uploaded diagnostic bundle to Drive (link in PD incident). No config rollback performed; we have logs from 07:20-09:00. I'm keeping the diversion active and monitoring for 1h. If numbers remain stable we'll keep diversion and start a root-cause runbook.

-Tessa
Senior Ops Engineer
